project_requirements.title: What the call wants
project_requirements.question: What must the project address, develop and achieve?

cards.title: Central object
cards.question: What is the principal thing the project must develop?
cards.answer:
An SME's own product, process or digital solution for the solar, offshore wind or energy grid supply chain, developed close to market within six months.
Strand B is the bottom-up open part of the second RENEW-BOOSTER call (RENEW-BOOSTER is an EU-funded cluster project that passes part of its grant on to SMEs). Unlike Strand A, there are no predefined challenges: the SME proposes its own innovation. It must be at TRL 6–7 (a prototype shown in a realistic setting) and reduce dependence on critical raw materials, diversify supply chains or support the green and digital transition.
cards.sources:
Call_text_RENEW-BOOSTER_Call_2.pdf · pp. 2–3 · Scope and objectives of the call
Call_text_RENEW-BOOSTER_Call_2.pdf · p. 8 · Strand B – Open calls

cards.title: Scope
cards.question: Which activities fall within the funding opportunity's scope?
cards.answer:
Product innovation and supply chain diversification within the photovoltaics, offshore wind or energy grids value chains; anything outside these three is ineligible.
- Energy networks: SF6-free equipment (switchgear without the greenhouse gas SF6), advanced power cables made from recycled materials, tools to optimise energy infrastructure, systems that model, monitor and forecast cable health, and smart grid solutions such as dynamic line rating and predictive maintenance.
- Offshore wind, especially floating: turbine components and floating platforms, electrical and transmission solutions including cables, substations and offshore grid technologies, materials and manufacturing that use fewer critical raw materials, and solutions for installation, operation and maintenance.
- Photovoltaics: new cells, modules and materials, plant architectures, recyclability and power electronics.
- Cross-sector: AI, quantum computing, blockchain and digital twins to optimise energy and environmental performance, energy management systems, predictive analytics and environmental assessment tools.
Excluded: proposals outside the three value chains, proposals that do not match the strand's objectives, and activities that cause significant environmental harm.
cards.sources:
Call_text_RENEW-BOOSTER_Call_2.pdf · pp. 2–3 · Scope and objectives of the call
Call_text_RENEW-BOOSTER_Call_2.pdf · p. 5 · Ineligible proposals

cards.title: Problem
cards.question: What type of problem or need must justify the project, and where must it originate?
cards.answer:
The project must address Europe's exposure to critical material dependencies and supply chain bottlenecks in clean energy technologies.
The call text names wind, solar, grids and energy storage as technologies where recent disruptions and geopolitics have shown this weakness. The need is framed at the level of European industry and society; the applicant SME must also show a concrete market need and a credible route to commercial use. Every proposal must explicitly reference its alignment with the Critical Raw Materials Act and/or the Net-Zero Industry Act (EU laws on secure raw material supply and on manufacturing clean technologies in Europe), for example a CO2 or resource saving or moving part of a value chain into the EU.
cards.sources:
Call_text_RENEW-BOOSTER_Call_2.pdf · pp. 2, 4 · Background and policy context; Scope and objectives of the call
Call_text_RENEW-BOOSTER_Call_2.pdf · p. 13 · Evaluation criteria (Impact)

cards.title: Deliverables
cards.question: Which concrete outputs must the project produce?
cards.answer:
A tangible result, such as a prototype, demonstration or deployment, plus a mandatory final deliverable with an impact assessment.
The call expects tangible results within a short implementation period. Funding levels can be combined in sequence (prototype, then demonstration, then deployment), leading to a proof of concept or deployment. The final deliverable (slides, technical report or KPI summary) must contain measured or well-justified estimated results and the earnings or savings on the targeted indicators, such as cost reduction, efficiency gains or reduced dependency.
cards.sources:
Call_text_RENEW-BOOSTER_Call_2.pdf · pp. 2, 8 · Scope and objectives of the call; Strand B – Open calls
Call_text_RENEW-BOOSTER_Call_2.pdf · p. 12 · Final deliverable requirements

cards.title: Impact
cards.question: Which wider system outcomes and impacts must the project support?
cards.answer:
The project must strengthen the resilience and diversity of European PV, offshore wind and grid supply chains and support the green or digital transition, with measurable indicators.
The Impact criterion scores the contribution to supply chain resilience or diversification in these value chains, the green or digital benefits, market relevance with a credible plan for commercialisation, and measurable outcomes with clear indicators. The call links this to the Net-Zero Industry Act target that at least 40% of net-zero technology manufacturing, including electricity grid technologies, takes place in the EU, and to the Critical Raw Materials Act, citing materials such as silica, neodymium and copper. It sets no numeric target per project.
cards.sources:
Call_text_RENEW-BOOSTER_Call_2.pdf · p. 4 · Scope and objectives of the call (CRMA and NZIA)
Call_text_RENEW-BOOSTER_Call_2.pdf · p. 13 · Evaluation criteria (Impact)

cards.title: After the project
cards.question: How must the result be replicated, taken up and kept in use after the project?
cards.answer:
The result must be aimed at market uptake, not an isolated pilot: proposals must show a credible plan for commercialisation or deployment.
The call targets SMEs that are close to market uptake and asks for evidence of market relevance and uptake potential. Replication does not have to happen during the project. Beyond the grant, the project offers training, mentoring, matchmaking and access to clusters and customers. The call sets no requirements on standards, interoperability or who must operate the result after the project.

cards.title: Number of partners
cards.question: What is the permitted or required consortium size?
cards.answer:
One to three SMEs: an SME may apply alone or in a consortium of up to three SMEs.
No minimum consortium is required.
cards.sources: Call_text_RENEW-BOOSTER_Call_2.pdf · p. 5 · Consortia

cards.title: Partner composition
cards.question: Which types of partners must the consortium include?
cards.answer:
Only SMEs from the EU-27 or other Single Market Programme countries; no other organisation types can be partners.
Each partner must meet the EU SME definition (fewer than 250 staff and turnover up to EUR 50 million or balance sheet up to EUR 43 million, counting group companies where relevant) and have no conflict of interest with the RENEW-BOOSTER partners. At least 10% of funded SMEs should come from countries other than the project partners' (Denmark, Norway, Poland, France, Bulgaria and Spain), so Dutch SMEs count towards this share.

cards.title: Distribution of work
cards.question: How must work and budget be distributed among partners?
cards.answer:
The lead SME receives the money and distributes it under a consortium agreement; every funded SME must provide its own co-funding.
Partners are jointly responsible for the proper use of funds and may be jointly liable under the funding agreement. Each SME may receive at most EUR 60,000 across all RENEW-BOOSTER calls.

cards.title: Coordinator
cards.question: What type of organisation may or must act as lead applicant?
cards.answer: An eligible SME; in a consortium, one of the SMEs acts as coordinator and submits the application.

project_requirements.title: TenneT's position
project_requirements.question: What is TenneT's position within the consortium?

cards.title: Coordinate
cards.question: Can TenneT apply or coordinate, and under which conditions?
cards.answer:
No. Only SMEs may apply and coordinate, and TenneT TSO B.V. is a large company, not an SME.
The call admits only enterprises with fewer than 250 staff and turnover up to EUR 50 million or a balance sheet up to EUR 43 million.
cards.sources: Call_text_RENEW-BOOSTER_Call_2.pdf · p. 4 · Eligibility criteria (Applicant type and SME status)

cards.title: Participate
cards.question: Can TenneT take part without receiving funding?
cards.answer:
Not as a formal partner, but TenneT could support an SME applicant from outside, for example as a pilot site or with a letter of intent.
The call allows only SMEs in a consortium, so TenneT cannot join one. It does expect new suppliers and diversified supply chains to be validated through pilot testing, and it scores market relevance and uptake potential. This leaves room, in my interpretation, for a grid operator to host a pilot, provide test conditions or data, or confirm interest as a future customer. The call itself does not define such a role, so TenneT would act only through its agreement with the SME.
cards.sources:
Call_text_RENEW-BOOSTER_Call_2.pdf · p. 3 · Examples of eligible innovations include
Call_text_RENEW-BOOSTER_Call_2.pdf · p. 5 · Consortia

cards.title: Receive funding
cards.question: Can TenneT receive funding, and which funding rate or cost rules apply?
cards.answer:
No. The financial support goes only to eligible SMEs, so TenneT must finance any contribution it makes itself.
The call has no Dutch national rules or separate rate for large companies.

project_requirements.title: Innovation
project_requirements.question: What type of innovation must the project develop?

cards.title: Innovation threshold
cards.question: Must the project produce genuinely new knowledge or technology, or may it integrate and apply existing solutions?
cards.answer:
The solution must be new or clearly improved compared with what exists, but it may build on and apply existing technology.
The Excellence criterion scores the level of innovation and ambition, including novelty and added value. Eligible examples include new or improved products and services that replace critical materials, new suppliers validated through pilots, process innovations and digital solutions for supply chain monitoring and traceability.
cards.sources:
Call_text_RENEW-BOOSTER_Call_2.pdf · p. 3 · Examples of eligible innovations include
Call_text_RENEW-BOOSTER_Call_2.pdf · p. 12 · Evaluation criteria (Excellence)

cards.title: Innovation object
cards.question: In what must the project innovate?
cards.answer:
Mainly in technology, products and manufacturing processes, with digital solutions and business models also allowed.
The FAQ lists technologies, products, services and business models. The call text names product innovation, process innovation in manufacturing, and digital tools such as AI, digital twins, predictive analytics and energy management systems.

cards.title: Development stages
cards.question: Which development stages must the project cover?
cards.answer:
Late-stage development: validation, demonstration and deployment of a solution, not research.
The three grant levels (EUR 10,000, 30,000 and 60,000) correspond to increasing project maturity and can be combined in sequence, from prototype to demonstration to deployment, leading to a proof of concept or deployment.

cards.title: Maturity
cards.question: Which maturity level is expected at the start and end of the project?
cards.answer:
Projects should be at TRL 6–7 (a prototype shown in a realistic or operational setting); the FAQ says around TRL 6 and up.
The call sets no required end level for Strand B.

project_requirements.title: Work
project_requirements.question: Which activities or work structure must the project cover?

cards.title: Demonstration
cards.question: Where and under which conditions must the solution be demonstrated?
cards.answer:
The call does not prescribe a test environment, but it expects validation through pilot testing for new suppliers and diversified supply chains.
It leaves the choice of laboratory, pilot or real operating conditions to the applicant, within a project of at most six months.

cards.title: Integration
cards.question: How must the activities fit together and with existing systems?

cards.title: Evidence
cards.question: What must the demonstration prove?
cards.answer:
The project must prove its results with measurable indicators and report them in a final deliverable with an impact assessment.
The final deliverable must contain, at a minimum, measured or well-justified estimated results and the earnings or savings on the targeted indicators, such as cost reduction, efficiency gains, reduced dependency or shorter time to market. The Impact criterion also asks how the indicators will be assessed.

cards.title: User participation
cards.question: How must users take part in the project?

cards.title: Safety and cybersecurity
cards.question: Which safety, cybersecurity or data requirements must the project meet?
cards.answer:
No call-specific safety or cybersecurity rules; the only mandatory condition of this kind is the Do No Significant Harm principle.
Applicants must confirm through a self-check that the project does not seriously harm EU environmental objectives, for example through significant greenhouse gas emissions, pollution or damage to biodiversity.

funding_timing_submission.title: Funding
funding_timing_submission.question: How much funding can the project receive?

cards.title: Funding envelope
cards.answer:
SMEs can request EUR 10,000, 30,000 or 60,000, for a total project budget of about EUR 14,000 to 120,000.
- Total project size: about EUR 14,000 to 120,000 per proof of concept, including the SME's co-funding.
- Grant request: up to EUR 10,000, 30,000 or 60,000 depending on project maturity; at most EUR 60,000 per SME across all RENEW-BOOSTER calls; between 12 and 72 projects will be selected. The whole call (Strands A and B) has EUR 800,000.
- Funding form: financial support to third parties (cascade funding, where an EU-funded project passes money on to companies) through a sub-grant agreement with the RENEW-BOOSTER consortium.
cards.sources:
Call_text_RENEW-BOOSTER_Call_2.pdf · p. 8 · Strand B – Open calls
EU Funding & Tenders Portal, RENEW-BOOSTER Eurocluster Call N°2 · General information (Total funding available)

cards.title: Funding rate and co-financing
cards.answer:
Each funding level requires private SME co-funding of about 30% to 50%, rising with the grant size.
- Co-financing conditions: co-funding must be the SME's own money or debt; in-kind contributions, personnel costs, salaries and staff time do not count. It applies to each funded SME in a consortium.
- Evidence required: the SME must show at application that it can provide the co-funding and document it at reporting; applications without a completed co-funding table are not funded.
The exact rate per grant level is shown only in an image (Graph 2) in the call text, which could not be read as text.
cards.sources:
Call_text_RENEW-BOOSTER_Call_2.pdf · pp. 6, 8 · Co-funding requirements & budget allocation; Strand B – Open calls
Call_text_RENEW-BOOSTER_Call_2.pdf · p. 11 · Co-funding and grant amounts (indicative)

cards.title: Budget constraints
cards.answer:
Applicants must submit separate grant and co-funding budget tables; depreciation is not eligible.
- Eligible costs: equipment and materials, software and licences, personnel costs (grant budget only), external services and justified subcontracting, other project costs.
- Caps or mandatory allocations: EUR 60,000 per SME across all RENEW-BOOSTER calls.
- Excluded costs: depreciation of existing or new equipment, costs unrelated to the project, and costs already funded by other public sources.
- Overheads and VAT: VAT is eligible only if it cannot be recovered.
- Subcontracting or equipment: subcontracting must be necessary and consistent with the work plan and budget.
cards.sources: Call_text_RENEW-BOOSTER_Call_2.pdf · pp. 6–7 · Eligible Costs; Ineligible Costs

funding_timing_submission.title: Timing
funding_timing_submission.question: What timing should the proposal submission and project follow?

cards.title: Application route
cards.answer:
One stage: a single application through EU Survey by 30 November 2026, 17:00 CET.
- Stage 1 — Application: 30 November 2026, 17:00 CET; online EU Survey form in English within each text box's character limit; open to single SMEs or consortia of up to three SMEs, with one application per SME in this strand. Applications can be saved and edited until the deadline.
cards.sources:

cards.title: Project window
cards.answer:
A project lasts 3 to 6 months from the signature of the sub-grant agreement, expected at the end of January 2027.
- Maximum duration: 6 months.
- Required start: on signature of the sub-grant agreement (the contract between the SME and the RENEW-BOOSTER consortium), indicatively end of January 2027.
cards.sources: Call_text_RENEW-BOOSTER_Call_2.pdf · pp. 8, 10 · Strand B – Open calls; Timetable and deadlines

cards.title: Decision and contracting
cards.answer:
Results in mid-January 2027 and contracts at the end of January 2027 (both indicative).
- Expected invitation or assessment result: evaluation in December 2026, results in mid-January 2027 (indicative).
- Grant agreement: contract signature at the end of January 2027 (indicative).
cards.sources: Call_text_RENEW-BOOSTER_Call_2.pdf · p. 10 · Timetable and deadlines

funding_timing_submission.title: Application
funding_timing_submission.question: Mandatory information to include in the application

cards.title: Mandatory submission package — pass/fail
cards.answer:
A complete EU Survey application in English with both budget tables and a registered PIC; incomplete applications may be rejected.
- Application form: EU Survey online form, in English, within the character limits; no annexes beyond those asked for on the platform.
- Budget: a grant budget table and a co-funding budget table, plus a work plan.
- Mandatory annexes: signed declarations where applicable, a Financial Identification Form and a Do No Significant Harm self-declaration.
- Registration: a 9-digit Participant Identification Code (PIC) on the EU Funding & Tenders Portal for every applicant SME.
cards.sources:
Call_text_RENEW-BOOSTER_Call_2.pdf · pp. 6, 10, 14 · Eligible Costs; Do No Significant Harm (DNSH) – mandatory principle; How to apply

cards.title: Evaluation and selection — scored or ranked
cards.answer:
Three criteria scored out of 10 each, with at least 6 needed on every criterion; proposals are ranked by total score within the budget.
- Evaluation criteria: Excellence (novelty, technical soundness, fit with Strand B), Impact (supply chain resilience in PV, offshore wind or grids, green or digital benefits, market uptake, measurable indicators), Quality and efficiency of implementation (work plan, team, budget, risk management).
- Thresholds: 6 out of 10 per criterion; maximum 30 points.
- Ranking rules: ties are broken by Impact, then Excellence, then Implementation, then geographical balance; at least 10% of funded SMEs must come from regions outside the partners' countries, with attention to the EU-13 (the countries that joined the EU from 2004 onwards).
- Budget assessment: budget adequacy and cost-effectiveness are scored; the consortium may leave funds unawarded or move them between strands.
cards.sources:
Call_text_RENEW-BOOSTER_Call_2.pdf · pp. 12–14 · Evaluation criteria and selection process; Tie-breaking procedure; Evaluation workflow
EU Funding & Tenders Portal, RENEW-BOOSTER Eurocluster Call N°2 · Further information

cards.title: Conditional and exceptional requirements
cards.answer:
The final payment depends on a final deliverable with an impact assessment and a feedback questionnaire.
- Conditional — final payment: a final deliverable with measured or estimated results and savings, plus the completed Single Market Programme feedback questionnaire; without it there is no final payment.
- Conditional — non-compliance: payments may be suspended if milestones or reports are missed.
- Exception — applying to both strands: an SME may also apply to Strand A, but only for distinct activities and without double funding.
- Recommended: the call encourages applicants to read the FAQ and contact the helpdesk; a recorded applicant webinar is available.
